accepted_phrases: Chocolate bloom is a whitish coating: fat bloom involves changes in fat crystals and sugar bloom involves moisture acting on sugar. The general source says bloom damages appearance and can make surface texture unappetizing without limiting shelf life, and describes bloomed chocolate as generally still edible. This classification does not prove cheap ingredients, authenticate an exact lot, or rule out contamination, allergens, package damage or a separate spoilage process. Tempering promotes glossy chocolate, snap, smooth texture and bloom resistance through controlled cocoa-butter crystallization, but the general mechanism does not verify the tempering history, crystal state or future result of any captured offer.

The pocket-melt thread reports one foil-wrapped chocolate egg becoming gooey after several hours in a jeans pocket. The snack-bag thread recommends opening a bag, pushing air out and clipping it for travel, while a reply warns that opening replaces a nitrogen-rich headspace with oxygen and can accelerate staling. The labeling thread recommends marking decanted or stored containers to preserve identity and date information. The Boston thread asks where to buy block chocolate for bark and contains local, historical suggestions and preferences. These statements motivate heat-excursion logging, original-seal preservation, lot/date labeling and current local verification, but none is a controlled ten-week trial or evidence about the exact five offers.

Autoxidation is oxygen-driven gradual degradation of organic compounds at ambient temperatures and can cause food rancidity through a free-radical chain process, but it supplies no exact nut-lot rate, induction time, package barrier or ten-week outcome. MVTR measures water-vapor passage and is strongly conditional on temperature, humidity gradient, thickness and method; sheet values do not establish whole-package performance because seams, creases, access points, heat seals and closures matter. OTR measures oxygen passage over time and likewise requires an exact material or complete-package test, with seals, joints and closures included. Generic mechanism pages cannot rank these five packages.

The five frozen seller pages establish offer assertions rather than ten-week performance. Hershey SKU B01M68WYTJ is 6.87 dollars with no reviews shown; its title and quick look describe one 3.6-ounce pack of eight individually wrapped 45-percent-cocoa snack-size bars, while Product Dimensions reports 1.41 ounces. West End Foods SKU B075V1Y762 is 79.99 dollars with no reviews shown and its selected title and quick look describe five pounds of Ghirardelli 60-percent cacao squares, hand-picked and packed by West End Foods, without independently proving an original unit wrapper or ten-week outcome. Blue Diamond SKU B0051TPWG2 is 7.70 dollars, rated 83 percent over twelve reviews, and describes one 14-ounce resealable bag of almonds covered in cocoa powder and dark-chocolate flavor rather than a plain chocolate bar. Second Nature SKU B0758FJ52X is 39.85 dollars with no reviews shown and describes twelve 4.5-ounce resealable pouches of dark chocolate with almonds, cashews and pecans, plus a warm-weather shipping caution, while Product Dimensions reports only 4.5 ounces. Oh Nuts SKU B00C6ALV0U is 21.99 dollars, rated 85 percent over twelve reviews, and has a selected 2-pound offer with freshness and zip-lock claims while Package Dimensions reports 1.2 pounds. Exact delivered variants, net quantities, lots, dates, labels and package states remain unresolved.

Before committing to a rural stash, verify the exact SKU and selected variant, delivered unit count and net mass, current price and shipping, lot and best-before information, ingredients and allergens, manufacturer storage instructions, original wrapper or seal, package construction when available, and remedy terms. Preserve independent sealed units, label receipt and opening dates, and calculate waste-adjusted delivered cost per serving that remains acceptable at week ten. A large bag or five-pound bundle creates more exposure and waste risk than multiple independent units unless exact packaging and observed retention offset that commitment; sticker price, bulk mass, rating, resealability and seller freshness copy do not decide the comparison.

Use the smallest reversible quantities and randomly allocate separate same-lot sealed units to weeks 0, 2, 6 and 10 when possible. Log pantry temperature, relative humidity and heat or moisture excursions; inspect identity, lot, date and seal before opening; photograph and separately classify bloom, package damage and other visible defects; smell before tasting and stop under predeclared safety or package-integrity rules. Record standardized aroma, snap or crispness, texture, stale or rancid notes, flavor and overall acceptability against a week-zero form-specific baseline. If matched current samples exist, code and randomize them for a paired or other discrimination test, but use separate acceptability scoring for preference and do not interpret a failure to detect difference as equality. Cross-product or cross-package causal claims require matched recipe, lot, storage and test conditions.

Combine the literal offer audit, bloom and tempering boundary, autoxidation and package-measurement boundary, community operational variables, independent-unit rotation accounting and staged sensory protocol into one decision table. For each exact verified configuration, mark identity, package integrity, declared storage, week-ten acceptability and waste-adjusted delivered cost as pass, fail or unresolved. Do not let a pass on one axis compensate for a safety stop, package failure or unresolved exact identity, and do not rank products that were not tested under comparable declared conditions.

The packet supports no immediate ten-week product winner. Treat bloom, tempering, autoxidation, MVTR, OTR and sensory discrimination as bounded mechanisms; retain seller quantity conflicts and forum scope; and verify every exact offer and package state. Begin with the smallest independent-unit commitment, run the declared week 0, 2, 6 and 10 protocol, and compare waste-adjusted delivered cost per accepted serving. Choose only the least-commitment exact configuration that passes identity, package, condition, week-ten sensory and waste-cost gates; if none passes or material fields remain unresolved, shorten the stocking horizon or defer. Do not infer a universal brand, format, barrier or safety winner.

The packet does not prove an immediate ten-week winner. Choose only the least-commitment exact configuration that passes exact identity, package integrity, declared storage, week-ten sensory acceptability and waste-adjusted delivered-cost gates; otherwise shorten the stocking horizon or defer.

Start with independently sealed units, verify the exact delivered offer, run the predeclared week-zero through week-ten protocol, and select the lowest-commitment passing rotation or shorten the horizon or defer without a universal brand or package winner.

The packet contains five frozen seller snapshots, bounded bloom, tempering, autoxidation, MVTR, OTR and sensory-method context, and four scoped community discussions, but it lacks verified exact delivered lots and dates, complete package structures and barrier tests, declared ten-week environment histories and matched week-ten sensory outcomes.
Seller prices, ratings, review counts, masses, counts, wrapper, resealability and freshness wording remain frozen offer assertions rather than measured ten-week results.
The Hershey 3.6-ounce versus 1.41-ounce fields and the Oh Nuts selected 2-pound versus 1.2-pound fields remain unresolved until the exact delivered variants are checked.

Fat bloom involves fat-crystal change and sugar bloom involves moisture acting on sugar; bloom can harm appearance and texture without by itself proving cheapness, spoilage, contamination or universal unsafety.
Tempering and cocoa-butter polymorphism explain gloss, snap and bloom resistance but do not verify any exact offer's process history or future crystal state.
Autoxidation supplies a plausible oxygen-driven rancidity mechanism but not an exact lot rate, induction time, package result or ten-week prediction.
MVTR and OTR comparisons require exact package structure, opening state, temperature, humidity, thickness, method and whole-package seals, closures, creases and joints.
The pocket melt, bag clip, labeling and Boston sourcing discussions remain author-, product-, place- and time-scoped operational clues rather than controlled durability trials.
Verify SKU, variant, net quantity, unit count, lot, date, ingredients, allergens, storage instructions, seal condition, delivered cost and remedy terms before purchase or tasting.
Preserve separately sealed units, label receipt and opening dates, and avoid exposing the full stash during sampling.
Use discrimination testing only for matched current samples, use separate descriptive and acceptability measures, and do not treat failure to detect a difference as equality or preference.
Do not infer a causal package winner across unlike recipes, products, lots, opening states, storage histories or test conditions.
Compare delivered cost per serving that remains acceptable at week ten after waste and rotation risk rather than sticker price, total mass or rating alone.
Choose only the least-commitment exact configuration passing identity, package, condition, week-ten sensory and waste-cost gates; otherwise shorten the stocking horizon or defer.
A chalky white coating proves that the chocolate was made from cheap ingredients.
Any visible bloom means the chocolate has spoiled and must be treated as the same failure mode as rancid nuts.
The general bloom article proves that every white-coated exact lot is safe regardless of mold, allergens, contamination or package damage.
The general tempering mechanism proves how each captured chocolate was manufactured and guarantees its week-ten crystal form.
One chocolate egg melting in a pocket is a controlled ten-week pantry test of all five exact offers.
Opening a snack bag, squeezing it and adding a clip restores the unopened package atmosphere and barrier.
Writing a date on a container prevents oxidation and guarantees freshness.
A historical Boston comment proves the current rural price and availability of these exact offers.
The general autoxidation page establishes that the exact Oh Nuts or Blue Diamond lot will turn rancid at a known week.
A generic MVTR definition is enough to rank the five exact packages for ten-week moisture protection.
A generic OTR definition proves that resealable bags or individual wrappers have the best complete-package oxygen barrier.
A packaging-film value automatically equals whole-package performance even when seals, creases, joints, closures and opening state differ.
The Hershey page unambiguously establishes one net quantity despite its 3.6-ounce and 1.41-ounce fields.
The Oh Nuts page unambiguously establishes a two-pound delivered bag despite its 1.2-pound Package Dimensions field.
The Hershey seller's individually wrapped and lasting freshness wording proves good quality at week ten.
Five pounds and 60-percent cacao automatically make the reseller bundle the best stash value.
An 83-percent store rating over twelve reviews proves the Blue Diamond bag stays fresh for ten weeks.
Twelve resealable Second Nature pouches alone prove the exact delivered case will retain quality for ten weeks.
The zip-lock and no-more-rancid-nuts seller copy proves that the exact Oh Nuts lot cannot oxidize.
The lowest sticker price or largest total mass is the best value without accounting for delivered cost, accepted servings and waste.
Opening every unit at week zero has no effect on the validity or exposure risk of the ten-week trial.
Comparing unlike chocolate, flavored almonds and trail mix directly proves which package construction caused better retention.
Repeatedly opening and tasting the same package at weeks 0, 2, 6 and 10 is equivalent to sampling independent sealed timepoint units.
A discrimination test by itself quantifies preference, defect size and acceptability.
Failure to detect a difference proves that two products or timepoints are equal.
A ten-week result remains interpretable without recording pantry temperature, humidity, heat excursions, moisture excursions or opening state.
A sample with failed package integrity or a predeclared safety stop should still be tasted to complete the score sheet.
A low price can compensate for unresolved exact identity, failed package integrity or a safety stop.
The frozen packet already proves one unconditional brand, product or package winner for every ten-week rural pantry.
The buyer should commit to the largest bulk offer before verifying the delivered lot or running a reversible retention trial.

research_subgoals.description: Classify fat and sugar bloom, explain tempering and cocoa-butter crystal forms, and separate appearance and texture effects from cheapness, rancidity, contamination and universal safety claims.
Explain oxygen-driven autoxidation and the condition- and structure-specific meanings of MVTR and OTR without assigning exact rates or barrier rankings to the five offers.

Audit all five frozen seller offers, retain both quantity conflicts, distinguish product forms, and list every exact identity, lot, label, package, storage and delivered-cost field still requiring verification.
Keep the pocket melt, bag clip, storage-label and Boston sourcing discussions at their incident, author, product, place and time scopes while extracting only operational variables to test.

Design a smallest-commitment independent-unit rotation and week 0, 2, 6 and 10 protocol with environment logs, defect classification, safety stops, bounded discrimination, acceptability scoring and waste-adjusted cost.

Choose only a verified least-commitment configuration that passes every identity, package, condition, week-ten sensory and waste-cost gate, or shorten the horizon or defer without naming a universal winner.

query_requirements.text: Explain fat bloom, sugar bloom, tempering and cocoa-butter crystal behavior while refusing cheapness, spoilage and universal safety overclaims.
Explain autoxidation, MVTR and OTR and state the exact test conditions and whole-package features needed before making a ten-week package comparison.
Audit the five exact offers, preserve seller quantity conflicts, distinguish chocolate bars, cocoa-flavored almonds and trail mix, and identify unresolved exact-lot and package fields.
Use the four community discussions only as scoped operational clues about heat, opening, labeling and availability, not as exact-offer durability evidence.
Specify independent sealed timepoint units, environment and opening-state logs, week 0, 2, 6 and 10 checks, safety stops, sensory method limits and waste-adjusted cost per accepted serving.
Give a conditional least-commitment purchase, shorter-horizon or deferral decision without declaring an unconditional product, brand, package or safety winner.
